idea: The Persuasion Era Ended. The Prototype Era Started.
AI prototyping doesn't just speed up what gets built. It changes what gets attempted.
The best AI workflow is adversarial: two AIs that do not trust each other

The operators who survive the next model-recall cycle are not the ones with the best fallback model — they are the ones who built configuration artifacts that transfer across providers, because the durable asset was never the model.

Perplexity's ambition-expansion finding plus the Hokkaido farmer plus Argentina's non-human corporation law are the same signal: the builder economy just jumped from bits to atoms to legal personhood in 18 months, faster than any investor thesis predicted.

The Publicis-LiveRamp deal and the bot-traffic crossover are not two adtech stories: they are the same structural event, and publishers are about to discover that their identity infrastructure and their traffic measurement broke in the same quarter.

The 46x Cursor productivity gap and AWS AgentCore's Recommendations API are both symptoms of the same structural shift: configuration is becoming the new code, and the operators who treat agent briefs as IP artifacts will compound into a moat that model access cannot close.

The same week Anthropic's engineers stopped typing code and AWS shipped auto-refining agent prompts, the hardest unsolved problem in production AI fleets is not intelligence or infrastructure — it is verification, and the operators who build paranoid auditors before their competitors do will compound on everyone else's infrastructure investment.

Publicis buying LiveRamp and bot traffic crossing human traffic in the same quarter is not a coincidence — it is the simultaneous collapse of the two assumptions that the entire publisher identity stack was built on, and most publishers will not see either failure until Q3 reporting.

Dario Amodei is the first founder in tech history to publicly propose regulation that could ground his own product the same week he files for IPO — and that contradiction tells you more about the actual risk profile of frontier AI than any benchmark.
Stripe ran a 50-million-line Ruby migration in one day. The two-month estimate was the old world.
I run 14 agents. Half my ops pod exists to watch the other half. Nobody selling you a fleet tells you that.
The harness gap is the real reason Uber burned its Claude Code budget by April — and every operator who skips context infrastructure before scaling agents will hit the same wall.
The government recalled Anthropic's best model 72 hours after launch. Your workflow is now a national security risk.
